what: Step C1's report on the owner's iCloud account (the specification's 6.3 and 7.1): Q2 as the engine computes it beside the census's figure, and how many stream stories each grouping gives. Run by `engine/tests/live_screening.rs` on a copy of the store step B7 synced, made while B7's server ran: the database with SQLite's online backup, the log and the index as APFS clones. The copy was brought to schema 7 and every message derived again by the new derivation. Counts and milliseconds only: no address, subject, name, list id or text.
machine: the owner's Mac (Apple silicon, macOS), release build, Rust 1.98.0

upgrade.note: Opening the store runs migration 7 (new columns, the received date copied from `message`, four indexes, two tables) in 8 seconds. Every row is then stale (parser 2) and is derived again: 293 988 messages in 320 seconds alone, about 920 a second. Under `serve` a pass spends at most 30 seconds on it, so about 15 passes, some 75 minutes; until then the sender rows fill as the newest mail is derived first.

databaseBytes.note: Deriving every message again rewrites its rows, and the `link` table, which is most of the database, grew from 960 MiB packed to 1 236 MiB; `VACUUM` returns it, and the vacuumed copy is smaller than the store before the step. What step C1 adds: `recipient` (575 414 rows; 41 MiB as derived, 20 MiB packed), indexes of 12, 10, 8 and 4 MiB (`envelope_sender`, `envelope_sender_bulk`, `envelope_message_key`, `observation_mailbox`) and `sender` with its two indexes, under 1 MiB.

senders.showNote: Showing the sender of 272 217 messages counts them by mailbox and by list: about 0.42 seconds. Most senders have a few hundred messages or fewer.

q2.rule: Of inbound messages from senders the person never wrote to, the share with a list or bulk header or a template key seen at least five times (the specification's 7.2, rules 3 and 4). Written to: a message a sent mailbox has shown names the sender among its recipients.

groupingsNote: Stream stories are made of the bulk mail from strangers (rule 3). A story needs five messages. `byKey` groups by list id, or else by sender and template key; `byKeyAndShape` adds the body's shape; `bySender`, not one of section 8's groupings, groups by list id or else by sender alone. Without the largest mailbox, 7 329 bulk messages fall into 4 367 groups by key: a template key holds the subject's shape, so mail whose subject changes with each issue makes a group of one each time. By key 39% of that bulk mail is in a story, by key and shape 26%, by sender 81%. Which grouping makes stories is step C2's.

privacy.liveStoreFilesOpenToOthers: 48 index files the B7 server (built before the program set its mask to 077) wrote since step B7, inside directories only the owner can enter; closed to others again on 2026-11-14. The server that writes them is that build until it is restarted with a newer one
